There are two basic spheres of society -- economic and political. Of course, there is large overlap in the two, but the distinction is important.

The political spectrum is

Reactionary - Conservative -- Liberal - Radical

The economic spectrum is

Anarchy - Capitalism - Socialism - Communism, and separately Authoritarianism

or you could lump things together into a simpler economic spectrum

Rightist -- Leftist

Her analysis is pretty good, but I think it is far more economic than political -- which means her headings are wrong.

A better choice of headings, although not perfect, would be Relatively Right and Relatively Left

I added the "Relatively" because those are definitely not the far ends in most cases, but rather a comparative slice of the spectrum.

Radical usually refers to someone visionary, but, as per language confusion, can refer to the complete opposite.

A Radical in the usual sense would be the ultimate individual, not part of a collective.
